text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- The head of military intelligence expects more attacks: "Arafat is not making an effort to prevent terrorism".
- Chief rabbi decides to stop accepting payment for performing weddings after newspaper report.
- Jordan is demanding Israel return property confiscated under absentee laws.
JERUSALEM POST
- Military intelligence chief: Arafat okayed terror.
- Inner cabinet demands Palestinian Authority crack down on terror.
- Prime minister denies talking unity government with Peres.
- Eliyahu buys 36 percent stake in Ayalon Ins.
- Teva Medical, Israel International Fund, Taoz in joint venture.
- Bank Discount share offer slated for next month.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Assessment: Arafat wants to bring down Netanyahu's government.
- U.S. Ambassador Martin Indyk leaves post in the summer.
MAARIV
- Army sources: Palestinian security official Jibril Rajoub initiated weekend unrest in Hebron.
- Huge crowd at Apropo restaurant when it reopened on Sunday.
GLOBES
- Clal expected to report losses in fourth quarter of 1996.
- Bezeq officials pressing to appoint Hochman as phone company's permament director-general.
